hook.situation: You need to say that someone caused another person to eat, sleep, wear something, read aloud, sit down, laugh, cry, know something, or lower a level. The key is to separate the person doing the base action from the person or thing causing it.
objectives: Build natural causative pairs such as 먹다/먹이다, 자다/재우다, 입다/입히다, and 앉다/앉히다.
Choose between a lexical/morphological causative, V-게 하다, and V-게 만들다.
Avoid confusing causative forms with passive-looking forms such as 읽히다.
hook.whyItMatters: Causatives are not just grammar labels. They change the story: 아이가 먹었어요 means the child ate; 엄마가 아이에게 밥을 먹였어요 means the mother caused or helped the child eat.

grammarNotes.title: V-이/히/리/기/우/구/추-다 - lexical causative pairs
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Do not treat the seven suffixes as a machine you can attach to any verb. Learn the common pairs and always ask: who does the base action, and who causes it?
grammarNotes.formation: Some Korean causatives are built into the verb with a suffix: 먹다 -> 먹이다, 자다 -> 재우다, 입다 -> 입히다, 앉다 -> 앉히다, 웃다 -> 웃기다, 울다 -> 울리다, 낮다 -> 낮추다. The causer is usually the subject. The person affected can appear with 에게/한테 or 을/를 depending on the verb: 아이에게 밥을 먹이다, 학생들을 앉히다, 모두를 웃기다. Some forms, especially 읽히다, can be passive-like or causative depending on the sentence, so context matters more than the suffix shape.

examples.note: The child eats; the mother causes or helps it.

examples.en: The father put the baby to sleep.
The staff seated the guest by the window.
examples.note: 앉다 is intransitive; 앉히다 takes the person being seated.

exceptions: 읽히다 is the warning example: 선생님이 학생들에게 본문을 읽혔어요 is causative, but 책이 잘 읽혀요 is text-focused/passive-like.

grammarNotes.title: V-게 하다 - have or make someone do something
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use V-게 하다 when there is no natural lexical causative, or when you want a clearer, more flexible 'have someone do V' sentence.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach 게 하다 to the action you want someone to do: 읽게 하다, 공부하게 하다, 기다리게 하다. The caused person can be marked by 을/를 or 에게 depending on the sentence. Compared with lexical causatives, V-게 하다 is more transparent and works with many verbs.

examples.en: The teacher had the students read the passage.
My parents made me sleep early.
examples.note: Same idea as 재우다, but more analytic.

examples.en: The team lead had the staff sit in the front seats.
The company made the employees work overtime.
examples.note: Useful when there is no single lexical causative.

grammarNotes.title: V-게 만들다 - cause a result, often emotionally or forcefully
grammarNotes.mentalModel: V-게 만들다 focuses on the resulting state. It often feels stronger or more emotional than V-게 하다.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach 게 만들다 to the result: 울게 만들다, 웃게 만들다, 생각하게 만들다, 포기하게 만들다. Use it when the cause is a situation, movie, words, pressure, or experience that drives someone into a result. It can sound heavier than V-게 하다, so do not use it for every simple instruction.

examples.note: Emotional result; compare with 저를 울렸어요.

examples.en: Those words made the atmosphere awkward.
The difficult problem made the students think.
examples.note: The problem causes the mental action.

examples.en: The long meeting made everyone exhausted.
examples.note: A situation creates an unwanted result.

exceptions: For a direct instruction, V-게 하다 is usually cleaner: 선생님이 학생들에게 읽게 했어요. Use 만들다 when the result or emotional force matters.

exampleSentence.en: The mother gave the child medicine.
The father put the baby to sleep.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 아이가 밥을 먹었어요와 엄마가 아이에게 밥을 먹였어요는 다르죠?
lines.romanization: aiga babeul meogeosseoyowa eommaga aiege babeul meogyeosseoyoneun dareujyo?
lines.en: The child ate and the mother fed the child are different, right?

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 네. 먹었어요는 아이가 한 행동이고, 먹였어요는 엄마가 하게 한 행동이에요.
lines.romanization: ne. meogeosseoyoneun aiga han haengdongigo, meogyeosseoyoneun eommaga hage han haengdongieyo.
lines.en: Yes. Ate is what the child did; fed is what the mother caused to happen.
lines.grammarNote: The causer and doer are different.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 그럼 선생님이 학생들에게 본문을 읽혔어요도 사동이에요?
lines.romanization: geureom seonsaengnimi haksaengdeurege bonmuneul ilkyeosseoyodo sadongieyo?
lines.en: Then is 'the teacher had the students read the passage' also causative?
lines.grammarNote: 읽히다 can be causative in the right sentence.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 맞아요. 하지만 책이 잘 읽혀요는 사동보다 피동처럼 느껴져요.
lines.romanization: majayo. hajiman chaegi jal ilkyeoyoneun sadongboda pidongcheoreom neukkyeojyeoyo.
lines.en: Right. But 'the book reads well' feels more passive-like than causative.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 웃기다와 울리다는 감정이 바뀌는 사동으로 보면 되겠네요.
lines.romanization: utgidawa ullidaneun gamjeongi bakkwineun sadongeuro bomyeon doegenneyo.
lines.en: So I can see utgida and ullida as causatives where emotions change.

readingText.title: 누가 하게 만들었는지 보기
readingText.body: 사동사를 공부할 때는 접미사만 외우면 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 먼저 누가 실제 행동을 하는지 보고, 그다음 누가 그 행동을 하게 했는지 확인해야 해요. 아이가 밥을 먹으면 아이가 행동의 주체예요. 하지만 엄마가 아이에게 밥을 먹이면 엄마가 사동의 주체이고 아이가 먹는 사람이에요. 선생님이 학생들에게 본문을 읽혔어요는 학생들이 읽지만 선생님이 읽게 한 문장이에요. 반대로 책이 잘 읽혀요는 책이 쉽게 읽힌다는 뜻이라 사동보다 피동처럼 느껴져요. 그래서 먹이다, 재우다, 입히다, 앉히다 같은 단어는 기본형과 짝으로 외우는 것이 좋아요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: When studying causative verbs, memorizing only suffixes can be confusing. First check who actually performs the action, and then who causes that action to happen. If a child eats rice, the child is the doer. But if a mother feeds the child, the mother is the causative subject and the child is the one eating. In 'the teacher had the students read the passage,' the students read but the teacher caused it. By contrast, 'the book reads well' means the book is easy to read, so it feels more passive-like than causative. That is why words like 먹이다, 재우다, 입히다, and 앉히다 are best memorized as pairs with their base forms.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 사동사를 공부할 때 먼저 무엇을 확인해야 해요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 누가 실제 행동을 하는지 확인해야 해요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 엄마가 아이에게 밥을 먹이면 누가 밥을 먹어요?
책이 잘 읽혀요는 사동보다 무엇처럼 느껴져요?

culturalNote.title: Caregiving, Classroom, Workplace
culturalNote.body: Korean causatives appear most naturally in roles where someone guides another person's action: parents feed children, teachers have students read, staff seat guests, managers make employees work, and stories make people laugh or cry. If the sentence sounds too forceful with V-게 만들다, switch to V-게 하다 or a lexical causative such as 앉히다.
culturalNote.tip: Before choosing the form, name three roles in English: causer, person affected, base action. Then build the Korean sentence.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence means the mother fed the child?
inlineExercises.explanation: 먹이다 means someone causes or helps another person eat.
The teacher causes the students to read. 책이 술술 읽혔어요 is passive-like/text-focused.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which form is better for a strong emotional result?
inlineExercises.explanation: V-게 만들다 fits emotional or resultative causation.

bullets: Base action: 먹다, 자다, 입다, 앉다, 웃다, 울다.
Lexical causative: 먹이다, 재우다, 입히다, 앉히다, 웃기다, 울리다, 알리다, 낮추다.
V-게 하다 is flexible and neutral; V-게 만들다 highlights a result or emotional force.
Always identify the causer, the affected person, and the base action before choosing the form.
